sources.name: WTO press release 252: WTO Ministerial Conference approves China's accession (10 November 2001)
World Bank World Development Indicators (GDP, GDP per capita, population)

steps.title: Bigger economies export more
text: Each dot is an economy in 2024, sized by population, with the [EU](EU) counted as one. Across **168** economies, goods exports and GDP line up almost perfectly on log scales: Pearson **r = 0.93**.
That is mostly about size. Large economies make more of everything, including things to sell abroad.

steps.title: Rich is not the same as big
text: Swap GDP for GDP **per person** and the pattern weakens to **r = 0.29**. Wealth tells you much less than size about how much a country exports.
[China](CHN) is the clearest case: the world's largest goods exporter in 2024 (**$3.58 trillion**), yet only 51st in GDP per person, at about **$13,300**.
Here China means the Chinese mainland; [Hong Kong](HKG) SAR and Macao SAR are separate dots. Turn on “China + HK & Macao” to combine them.

steps.title: 1995: already a major exporter
text: In 1995 [China](CHN)'s GDP per person was about **$610**, lower than in 117 other economies. It still ranked 6th by exports, at **$149 billion**.
The [EU](EU) ($815 billion of exports outside the EU), the [US](USA) and [Japan](JPN) led.

steps.title: Thirty years in one motion
text: The WTO approved [China](CHN)'s membership in November 2001. Watch China's dot climb up and to the right.

China's exports overtook the [US](USA) in **2007** and the [EU](EU)'s exports to the rest of the world in **2014**. By 2024 they were **24 times** their 1995 value, and GDP per person had risen about **22 times** in current dollars.
[Vietnam](VNM) follows a similar path a step behind: from 44th to 15th by exports.

steps.title: Exports matter less to China than they did
text: As a share of GDP, [China](CHN)'s goods exports peaked at **35%** in 2006. By 2019 they were down to **17%**, and in 2024 they stood at **19%**: the domestic economy grew even faster than exports.

Some economies depend far more on goods exports: [Vietnam](VNM) at **82%** of GDP and [Singapore](SGP) at **88%**, against **7%** for the [US](USA). But small does not simply mean open: across all economies the link is weak and, if anything, positive (r = 0.27 in 2024), because many of the smallest, such as the Pacific island states on the left, export few goods at all.

steps.title: Explore further
text: Pick other metrics from the axis menus, choose a product such as **Semiconductors & integrated circuits**, or click any dot to open that economy's panel. Correlation across economies does not show cause and effect.
